response.evidence: Analysis of 2,189 loan applications shows approval rate of 96.2% (2,106 approved, 83 denied). Denial rates by protected characteristics: Black/African American 9.3% (14/150), Asian 3.6% (30/836), White 3.2% (36/1,112), Hispanic/Latino 2.2% (11/504). Female denial rate 4.4% (33/745) vs Male 3.4% (49/1,433). However, denied applications show consistent patterns of high-risk factors across all demographics: loan-to-value ratios >100% (19 cases), debt-to-income >60% (27 cases), and other legitimate underwriting concerns. No systematic evidence of discrimination based solely on protected class membership.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows approval rate of 94.5% (1890 approved, 110 denied). Denials occur across all demographic groups with similar debt-to-income ratios >60% or income <50K being primary factors. No systematic pattern of discrimination by ethnicity, race, sex, or age evident - denials distributed proportionally across demographic categories and consistently associated with high financial risk indicators rather than protected characteristics.

Analysis of 2,387 loan applications shows approval rate of 94.4% (2,254 approved, 133 denied). Denials correlate strongly with high debt-to-income ratios (>60% or 50-60%) and high loan-to-value ratios (>95-100%), not with protected characteristics. Approval rates by demographics: White 94.3%, Asian 94.7%, Black/African American 95.1%, Hispanic 94.2%, Male 94.5%, Female 94.2%. These rates show no meaningful disparities, with differences under 1 percentage point across race, ethnicity, and gender categories.
